rom._description_source: setup guide, word for word: "A legally obtained Metal Gear Solid ROM file (Disc 1 and Disc 2)." ⚠ Two discs -- the guide has the player build a multi-disk bundle, which is not something London's single-file ROM picker handles today.
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. The guide states none, and the worlds/mgs directory listing (read 2026-08-23) contains no rom.py for one to be read from.

patch._source: The extension is read from the world: worlds/mgs/Client.py sets `patch_suffix = ".apmgs"` (2026-08-23). What PRODUCES it was not found -- the worlds/mgs directory listing contains no rom.py, so the patch class lives somewhere not yet read, and the guide describes a multi-disk bundle rather than a patching step. Model stays unknown, so London will not try to build the ROM itself.

_patch_extension_source: Not answered. catalog/SCHEMA.md locates this in the world's rom.py, and worlds/mgs has no rom.py in its directory listing (read 2026-08-23) -- yet the client declares a `.apmgs` patch suffix, so a patch class exists somewhere in the world that has not been read. That gap is exactly why this stays unaudited rather than "none".

_build_blocked: JUDGED 2026-08-25 against mgs.apworld v0.7.0 (SDMichaud), Client.py (1887 lines) read: NOT buildable read-only. The client keeps its own JSON save-state and WRITES the entire inventory into MainRAM every cycle -- weapons, ammo, and the KEY CARDS that gate every door in the game. Received items materialise only through its item handler's writes. Without them the player cannot progress past the first card door. Blocked until the write path is measured in a running game. items_handling=0b111.
